subject: Regional dimensioning request: Q1 dedicated pools for NovaCore
messages:
From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@novacore.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novacore.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T09:14:00Z
Subject: Initial ask: dedicated pools across regions for Q1 launch

Hi Olga & Rishi,

We’re lining up our Q1 launch and want to lock dedicated capacity commitments with Redwood so we have predictable latency and throughput during ramp. High level: 3-region footprint (US primary, EU for EU customers, APAC pilot). Our rough demand forecast is attached in the spreadsheet — it includes expected peak concurrent sessions and 95th pct response latency targets.

Can you help dimension minimum pool sizes per region given the model mix (quantized 70B LLMs + a smaller 13B reranker)? We’re aiming for a hard start-of-Q1 guarantee and would like an estimate for lead times and uplift buffer. Also flag any minimum term/commit thresholds that materially affect pricing.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

Tom
Tom Reed
Head of Product, NovaCore
From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reed <tom.reed@novacore.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask: dedicated pools across regions for Q1 launch

Tom —

Thanks for the spreadsheet, that’s very helpful. I pulled a short checklist and attached a capacity template (nova_capacity_template_v2.xlsx) so we can align on workload signals that drive sizing: session concurrency, median/95p token length, expected tokens/sec per session, and model routing mix.

Quick notes up front:
- We size pools conservatively by 30% buffer above your peak forecast for the first 90 days to absorb burst and onboarding inefficiencies.
- For mixed model workloads we recommend pinning a primary model per route to avoid cross-model cold-cache penalties.
- Lead time: US (4–6 weeks), EU (6–8 weeks for vendor/region capacity scheduling), APAC (8–12 weeks depending on zone).

Next steps: please fill the template fields highlighted in yellow and I’ll produce a region-by-region table with suggested instance equivalents (H100/A100 v2 equivalence) and cost delta for reserved vs burst-eligible capacity. I’ll also loop in capacity ops for lead-time confirmations.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@novacore.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask: dedicated pools across regions for Q1 launch

Tom/Olga —

I took a quick pass using the numbers in your sheet (concurrency = 2.4k global peak, routing: 70% 70B, 30% 13B). High-level proposal (back-of-envelope) for committed pool equivalents:

US (primary): 160 H100-equivalent GPUs reserved.
EU: 60 H100-equivalent GPUs reserved.
APAC (pilot): 40 H100-equivalent GPUs reserved, with an option to add 20 burst-capacity credits in month 2.

Rationale: the 70B quantized inference profile we expect to run at ~200–240 effective tokens/s per H100 under our runtime with batching. We assumed median request length ~120 tokens and a 95th tail that requires extra headroom; that drives the 30% buffer.

Notes and risks:
- If NovaCore expects several long-running sessions (>>300 tokens median) we should increase the US pool by +20 GPUs to maintain 95p latency SLOs.
- EU procurement timelines often require regional vendor confirmation for hardware mapping — tagging Marissa to confirm EU lead-time.

I’ll prepare a clean PDF table for the customer with cost deltas for reserved vs mixed reserved+burst pricing.

Rishi
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T14:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask: dedicated pools across regions for Q1 launch

Quick internal note — EU and APAC scheduling:

- EU: 6–8 weeks is feasible if we lock by end of November; we have a slot in the Amsterdam pool that can be carved.
- APAC: Singapore zone currently has constrained H100 inventory; realistic delivery to customer-facing dedicated pools is 10 weeks unless they accept H100-equivalent via a partner region for the first 6 weeks.
- Capacity ops recommends the staging window: provision soft-reserved VMs 2 weeks before start, run smoke tests, then promote to committed capacity on go-live.

Action for sales: if the customer signs a 12-month commit, finance can approve a 10% prepayment discount and shorter provisioning SLAs (we can tighten to 6 weeks EU / 8 weeks APAC in some cases).

Marissa
Head of Dedicated Capacity Programs, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Banerjee <priya@novacore.com>

Cc: procurement@novacore.ai, Tom Reed <tom.reed@novacore.ai>

Thanks — the sizing proposal looks reasonable. A few clarifications from procurement:

- We can commit to a 12-month term if pricing is within the attached SOW draft range. Please review SOW_NC-2026-143_draft.docx and confirm any non-standard cancellation clauses.
- For APAC pilot, we’d like the option to shift up to 30% of committed capacity between zones (SG -> Sydney) for the first 90 days with 72-hour notice. Is that an option?
- We want a clause for performance credits if 95p inference latency exceeds our target in any contiguous 7-day window.

Would appreciate a redlineable SOW and a DocuSign envelope to speed approval.

Best,
Priya
Director, Procurement — NovaCore

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into provisioning.
